prediction.the_claim_under_test: c12-profiled-fold measured the whole unpriced block in situ as the 15 device ops its per_device_op_s table holds outside the 8 census classes and generic_op: 2.0848 s, of which 2.0277 s maps to the 52 refused launch keys and 0.0571 s is an EmbeddingsDeviceOperation the launch-key census never recorded. This row tests that total with a second instrument built on different data.

directional_prediction.statement: the standalone sum over the 52 arms comes out AT OR ABOVE the in-situ 2.0277 s
directional_prediction.mechanism: c12-genericop-rate measured in situ 1.16-1.18x FASTER than every standalone arm on the same kernels (ship_in 1.2495 vs 1.0733 ms, ship_sdpa 1.4667 vs 1.2622, ship_out 0.4759 vs 0.4056), because a standalone arm carries its own dispatch and its own cache state. A standalone arm is therefore an UPPER bound on the in-fold cost.
directional_prediction.refutation: a standalone sum BELOW 2.0277 s refutes the direction and means one of the two instruments is wrong; that would be the finding and the table would stop.

prediction.addressable_prediction: the permute/transpose class is the block's largest single item at 0.5997 s in situ and it moves 108.8 GB over 12,696 calls, which is 181 GB/s against a measured DRAM roof near 440 GB/s. Predicted: it is NOT at the byte roof, so it is not excused by bandwidth, and it is far above the 5.60 us/call launch floor so it is not excused by launch either. That makes it the one item in this block that clears the 0.3 s speculative tier on its own.
